title: Selecting specific exception handlers and Distinguishing input failures from programming defects

blocks.text: An except handler matches its named exception class and subclasses. The first matching handler runs.
Put subclass-specific handlers before broader parent handlers so the specific recovery remains reachable.
FileNotFoundError is an OSError subclass. When recovery actions differ, except FileNotFoundError: must come before except OSError:.

annotations.text: Broader parent recovery comes later; first match wins.

segments.label: Place FileNotFoundError before a broader handler
segments.summary: Opening a file with an incorrect filename produces FileNotFoundError. A broad handler replaces the traceback with a missing-file message, but also gives that misleading message for an undefined name. Restricting the handler to FileNotFoundError leaves the NameError unmatched. Adding an Exception handler below it provides a separate, broader response. Putting that broader handler first would prevent the missing-file branch from running. Finally, binding the caught exception with as e allows its error message to be displayed.

bridge.before: Watch how a broad handler reports an undefined name as a missing file. The clip uses Exception as its broader handler; our example uses OSError to focus on the relevant parent–subclass relationship.
bridge.after: The clip demonstrates specific-before-broad ordering. The text also explains subclass matching and first-match selection, and supplies the relationship absent from the clip: FileNotFoundError is a subclass of OSError.

steps.title: Distinguishing input failures from programming defects

blocks.text: ValueError can identify unsuitable input, such as malformed numeric text. Reject or request correction of input that violates the stated value contract.
NameError means a local or global name cannot be found. Correct a misspelled implementation name rather than rejecting the supplied input.
PermissionError reports inadequate access rights for a filesystem operation. Report the access failure; do not assume the path or implementation is inherently wrong.

left.title: Distinguishing input failures from programming defects
left.alt_text: ValueError from int("three") → Request corrected numeric input

right.title: Distinguishing input failures from programming defects
right.alt_text: Two independent diagnostic mappings: NameError caused by a misspelled quantity name → correct the implementation name; PermissionError caused by inadequate access rights → report the access failure.

blocks.takeaway: Choose the response from the reported cause, not an assumption that every failure is bad input.
